c.pop: ~5,000 (village; broader area much smaller than a town)
c.tagline: A 5th-century sky palace atop a sheer 180-meter granite monolith, ringed by ancient water gardens and frescoes

card: Accepted at larger hotels; cash preferred at small guesthouses and vendors

taxi.fareNote: Tuk-tuks are the standard local transport; hiring a driver for the day is common for combining Sigiriya with nearby sites

emergency.note: 1990 is a free national ambulance service covering most of Sri Lanka

religion: Buddhism (majority, reflecting the site's historical monastic use)
walk: The rock fortress climb involves significant stairs and is best done early morning to avoid heat and crowds; Pidurangala and Dambulla require a tuk-tuk or car

safety.safety: Very safe, well-managed UNESCO site popular with families and history enthusiasts
safety.crime: Very low crime; the main caution is the exposed, sometimes vertigo-inducing summit staircase

hood_landmark.Sigiriya Village: The small village of guesthouses and restaurants near the site entrance
hood_landmark.Pidurangala Rock: Pidurangala Rock, the classic sunrise viewpoint of Sigiriya

avoid.reason: Politely decline the unofficial 'guides' and gem-shop touts near the rock entrance, and avoid driving rural roads at dusk when wild elephants cross.

hood_desc: The small settlement near the site entrance with most guesthouses, restaurants, and the site museum.
A neighboring rock a short drive or tuk-tuk ride away, climbed mainly for its unobstructed sunrise view of Sigiriya itself.

The resort belt along the Inamaluwa-Sigiriya road about five kilometres north-west of the rock, where the larger hotels sit in paddy and scrub with the rock on the horizon. Suits travellers who want a pool and space and do not mind a short drive to the entrance.

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water in Sri Lanka's Cultural Triangle.

transit.sys: Tuk-tuks around the village and to nearby sites
transit.map: Not centrally published; tuk-tuks and hired drivers cover the area
transit.note: Hiring a driver for the day is common for combining Sigiriya, Pidurangala, and Dambulla

transport.air: Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) near Colombo, about 3.5-4 hr away, is the main international gateway
transport.train: Nearest train station is Habarana, about 20 min away, connected by tuk-tuk
transport.bus: Buses connect to Dambulla, Kandy, and Colombo
transport.car: Well connected via the A6 and A11 highways; a private driver is a popular way to combine Sigiriya with the Cultural Triangle

airport.name: Bandaranaike International Airport, Colombo (main gateway)
airport.transport: Private car/driver, or train via Habarana plus tuk-tuk

net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels
net.ap: A Dialog or Mobitel tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is appreciated for guides and drivers
tip.r: 10% is standard, often added automatically at larger restaurants

food.name: Rice and curry
food.desc: The village meal: red rice ringed by eight or more small curries - dhal, jackfruit, beetroot, pumpkin, sambol and a fiery chicken or fish.

places.name: Priyamali Gedara
places.note: Home-style buffet cooked over firewood in a family compound; the classic Sigiriya village lunch.

places.name: Chooti Restaurant
places.note: Buffet-style local kitchen with a wide spread of curries, popular after the rock climb.

places.name: Sakura Restaurant
places.note: Long-running buffet and cooking-class spot with a generous vegetable curry line-up.

food.name: Hoppers and egg hoppers
food.desc: Bowl-shaped fermented rice-flour pancakes, lacy at the rim and soft in the middle, often with an egg cracked in and eaten with sambol.

places.name: Sigiriya junction street stalls
places.note: Evening hopper pans fire up by the roadside from about 5pm until the batter runs out.

places.name: Priyamali Gedara
places.note: Will cook hoppers to order for dinner alongside the curry spread if you ask ahead.

places.name: Athula Restaurant
places.note: Reliable local canteen doing hoppers and string hoppers with curry and sambol.

food.name: Kottu roti
food.desc: Godamba roti chopped on a hot griddle with egg, vegetables and meat to a metallic drumbeat you can hear down the street.

places.name: Sigiriya junction street stalls
places.note: Griddle shops start clattering at dusk - cheese kottu and chicken kottu are the standards.

places.name: Athula Restaurant
places.note: Among the most recommended local kitchens on the Dambulla road for kottu and rice.

places.name: Inamaluwa junction eateries
places.note: Roadside rice-and-kottu shops on the main highway junction, busy with drivers.

food.name: Curd with kithul treacle
food.desc: Thick buffalo curd served in a clay pot and drizzled with dark palm treacle - the standard dessert across the dry-zone villages.

places.name: Roadside curd stalls, Dambulla-Habarana road
places.note: Clay pots hang in rows outside village stalls; sold with a bottle of kithul syrup.

places.name: Priyamali Gedara
places.note: Finishes the village buffet with curd and treacle from local producers.

places.name: Dambulla Dedicated Economic Centre
places.note: Sri Lanka's biggest produce market - curd, treacle, jaggery and fruit at farm prices.

food.name: Polos and jackfruit curries
food.desc: Young jackfruit slow-cooked in dark roasted spices until it shreds like meat, with breadfruit and gotu kola sambol on the side.

places.name: Priyamali Gedara
places.note: Cooks jackfruit and forest vegetables the traditional way in clay pots over wood.

places.name: Chooti Restaurant
places.note: Vegetarian-friendly buffet where jackfruit and pumpkin curries appear most days.

places.name: Sigiriya Village Hotel restaurant
places.note: Hotel buffet that keeps a proper Sri Lankan section alongside international dishes.

food.name: Lamprais and roast paan breakfast
food.desc: Banana-leaf parcels of rice, curry and frikkadel, plus the everyday breakfast of coconut roti or bread with lunu miris and dhal.

places.name: Sigiriya guesthouse kitchens
places.note: Family guesthouses along the village road serve the best local breakfasts - order the night before.

places.name: Athula Restaurant
places.note: Morning roti, dhal and sambol before the drive to the caves or the rock.

food.name: Thambili (king coconut)
food.desc: Orange king coconuts hacked open at the roadside; sweet, faintly salty water drunk straight from the shell after the climb.

places.name: Sigiriya Rock entrance stalls
places.note: Carts at the ticket gate and car park - the standard reward for the 1,200 steps.

places.name: Inamaluwa junction stalls
places.note: Piles of king coconuts at the highway turn-off, cheaper than at the rock.

places.name: Dambulla Dedicated Economic Centre
places.note: Fruit market where thambili is sold by the sack alongside wood apple and mango.

food.name: Ceylon tea
food.desc: Strong local black tea taken with sugar and milk, or plain with ginger - poured from a battered flask at every village stop.

places.name: Chooti Restaurant
places.note: Pot of tea after the buffet, plus wood apple and passion fruit juices.

places.name: Sigiriya junction tea kiosks
places.note: Small kiosks pour plain tea and ginger tea for a few rupees all day.

places.name: Sakura Restaurant
places.note: Tea and fresh juices with the cave-temple lunch stop.

landmarks: Sigiriya Rock Fortress (Lion Rock)
A UNESCO-listed 5th-century palace-citadel atop a sheer 200-metre granite monolith, entered between colossal carved lion's paws, Sri Lanka's single most iconic sight.
Sigiriya Frescoes
Exquisite 1,500-year-old paintings of celestial maidens sheltered in a rock pocket halfway up the fortress, masterpieces of ancient Sinhalese art.
Mirror Wall
A polished ancient wall so finely plastered it once reflected the frescoes, inscribed with centuries of visitor graffiti poems dating from the 8th century.
Royal Water Gardens
Among the world's oldest landscaped gardens, a symmetrical spread of pools, fountains and moats still functioning at the foot of the rock.
Pidurangala Rock
The neighbouring monastic rock whose summit scramble delivers the classic dawn view of Sigiriya rising from the jungle.
Sigiriya Museum
A well-designed site museum explaining King Kashyapa's citadel through excavated artefacts, fresco replicas and a walk-through model of the rock.
Cobra Hood Cave
A dramatic boulder overhang shaped like a spread cobra's hood, bearing pre-Christian inscriptions and traces of ancient painted plaster.
Dambulla Cave Temple
A UNESCO-listed complex of five cave sanctuaries filled with 150 Buddha statues and vivid murals, twenty minutes from Sigiriya.
Minneriya National Park
Famous for The Gathering, when hundreds of wild elephants converge on the ancient Minneriya tank in the dry season, an unmissable nearby safari.
Ritigala Forest Monastery
Mysterious ruined meditation platforms and stone pathways of a 1st-century forest monastery hidden on a jungle-cloaked mountain reserve nearby.

train.note: Sigiriya has no railway station of its own. The nearest railheads are Habarana, about 17 km northeast on the Batticaloa/Trincomalee line, and Kekirawa roughly 30 km west, both served by Sri Lanka Railways (https://www.railway.gov.lk/) with trains from Colombo taking 4-5 hrs. From either station you finish the journey by bus or tuk-tuk, so most visitors skip the train and come by road from Dambulla. There is no international rail service anywhere in Sri Lanka.

bus.note: Dambulla, 25 km southwest, is the transport hub: buses run between Dambulla and Sigiriya roughly every 30 minutes from about 06:30 to 18:00 for around Rs 100. Coming from Polonnaruwa or Trincomalee you change at the Inamaluwa junction on the A6 and cover the last 10 km by local bus or tuk-tuk (about Rs 500). Long-distance buses from Colombo (~5 hrs) and Kandy (~3 hrs) terminate at Dambulla, and everything is paid in cash on board. No international coaches serve Sri Lanka.

ferry.note: Sigiriya is deep inland in the Cultural Triangle and has no ferry service; the surrounding reservoirs such as the Sigiriya Wewa are used for irrigation and wildlife, not transport.

half.name: Polonnaruwa
half.blurb: Medieval royal capital with stone-carved Buddha statues, brick stupas, and ancient reservoirs built by Sinhalese kings.

half.name: Kaudulla National Park
half.blurb: Wildlife reserve where wild elephant herds gather around a reservoir, especially during the dry season.

full.name: Kandy
full.blurb: Hill city built around a lake, home to the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic of the Buddha.

full.name: Anuradhapura
full.blurb: Ancient sacred city with centuries-old stupas and a bodhi tree said to be grown from a Buddha-era cutting.
